title: Extend a Capability Without Forking Nodics
readerIntent: Customize an existing capability in a customer project while preserving upgrades.
priorKnowledge: Know the owning capability and layer.
owner: Customer project module layered over an owning Nodics capability
summary: Prefer configuration, then a documented extension or override, and create new behavior only when the existing contracts cannot express the requirement.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
items: Search for an existing implementation, property, service, interceptor, pipeline node, event, schema extension, or route contract.
Configure existing behavior when only a supported choice or value changes.
Override or extend the smallest owning layer when behavior changes.
Keep the customization in the customer project module and preserve the original contract unless a versioned change is intentional.
Add a new framework mechanism only after a duplication and parallel-authority assessment.

sections.heading: Choose the smallest supported change
items: Data or policy value: use the owned configuration contract.
Additional declarative field or relationship metadata: use schema extension.
Business algorithm: extend or override the owning service.
Cross-service use case: extend the facade rather than duplicating services.
Lifecycle behavior: use a declared interceptor, pipeline, event, job, or workflow extension.
External technology: implement the provider interface behind the neutral capability.
New public behavior: add a versioned route only when no existing operation expresses it.

sections.heading: Project isolation
paragraphs: Customer customizations live in that customer's project repository and loader-visible module hierarchy. Two projects can provide different later implementations without either one modifying Nodics or affecting the other.
A reusable frontend such as Axis is deployed per customer project but remains presentation-only. Customer business customization belongs in the customer's backend project modules.

sections.heading: Example
paragraphs: If a project needs additional employee validation, extend the profile-owned validation or save-interceptor contract in the project layer. Do not copy the employee schema, create a direct database write, or validate only in Axis.

sections.heading: Detailed example
paragraphs: A logistics project requires a government identifier before activating a driver employee. Profile already owns Employee and activation. The project extends Employee through the supported schema layer and adds an owned validation interceptor reached by every activation mutation.
Imports, API calls, workflows, jobs, and Axis all encounter the same rule. The ecommerce project, which does not activate the logistics module, retains default Profile behavior.

sections.heading: Compatibility and upgrades
items: Preserve the public capability contract unless the change is intentionally versioned.
Call documented extension points rather than importing internal implementation files.
Record assumptions about schema fields, service methods, events, statuses, and configuration.
Regenerate derived artifacts after source-contract changes.
Run default behavior and project behavior tests during framework upgrades.
Document migration or deprecation when an extension point changes.

sections.heading: Duplication and authority review
items: Search existing services, facades, interceptors, pipelines, loaders, registries, workflows, events, providers, and configuration.
Confirm the proposed implementation does not create another data owner.
Confirm every mutation path reaches the same rule.
Confirm tooling and frontend code remain bridges rather than authorities.
Record why a new mechanism is required when extension is insufficient.

sections.heading: Required proof
items: Default behavior remains unchanged without the project module.
Customized behavior activates only in the intended project and scope.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, and regression tests pass.
Documentation explains the extension point, configuration, limitations, operations, and upgrade considerations.

sections.heading: Rollback and removal
paragraphs: A customization should be removable by deactivating its project module or governed configuration while default framework behavior remains intact. Data migrations and externally visible contract changes require a separate rollback or compatibility plan.
Unused experimental paths should be deprecated and removed once callers migrate; keeping both indefinitely increases ambiguity and test cost.
